messages:
maya: Heads-up: after yesterday's packing micro-opt we see a perf regression on INT8 weight-only paths. p50/p95/p99 up ~12/18/25% on short sequences (<=128) on a few test GPUs. Profiling points to pack/unpack time dominating for small batches.

samir: Can you paste numbers + profiler output? Is this only AWQ or GPTQ too?

maya: Quick paste of the benchmark (local rig: 1xA10, model=vicuna-13b-int8):
```
benchmark  --seq 32 --batch 1 --runs 100
baseline (old-pack): token/s=2100, p95=48ms, p99=72ms
new-pack-opt: token/s=1870, p95=57ms, p99=90ms
```
Flamegraph: https://internal-perf/reports/1759/pack-flame.svg (pack_cpu -> memcpy -> quantize kernels)

elena: Interesting. Is pack/unpack being done at request time or at model load? We should be packing once per model variant.

maya: Right now weight packing happens at load for static weights, but we added a fast-path that re-packs on first request for memory-layout normalization. That code path is serial and runs on the request thread.

samir: That explains it. If first-request repack is serial it will add tail latency for small batches. Two quick suggestions: 1) move repack to background thread + warm-up; 2) add a small LRU of packed buffers keyed by (model, qcfg, group_size).

maya: Agreed. Also seeing group_size sensitivity. With AWQ group_size=128 we get better quant quality but packing loops are smaller and more syscalls/copies. Increasing to 256 halves pack overhead but slightly degrades l2 loss on the 100 eval prompts we run.

elena: Can we measure pack-time vs group_size? I recall packing complexity ~O(N_weights * (1/group_size)) because we do per-group reproj.

maya: Did a microbench:
```
bench_pack.py --model vicuna-13b --q awq --group 128 -> pack=420ms
bench_pack.py --model vicuna-13b --q awq --group 256 -> pack=210ms
bench_pack.py --model vicuna-13b --q gptq --group 128 -> pack=620ms
bench_pack.py --model vicuna-13b --q gptq --group 256 -> pack=300ms
```
GPTQ pack is heavier (extra per-group ops) but GPTQ-packed runtime loop is slightly faster in generation for long sequences (better memory alignment).

perf-bot: [auto-bisect] Regression window 1759100000..1759200000 shows 8.3% median token throughput regression for int8-serving-small-batches. See: https://ci/reports/17592

samir: Two more angles: kernel selection/fallback. When pack formats change we sometimes trigger non-optimal kernel routes (scalar fallback) in the kernel chooser. Ensure packed-format ABI flags are consistent so runtime picks fused vector kernels. Also check that batching heuristics don't collapse small requests into pack-on-every-request scenarios.

maya: Good point. I saw kernel_chooser log lines like: `fallback_to_scalar=true` for some layers after pack change. Probably layout bit mismatch.

elena: Could be due to calibration differences between AWQ/GPTQ: quant zeros/scale placement affects alignment and causes some SIMD kernels to reject the weight blob. We should add a validator that rejects/rewrites pack header to advertise compatible features.

maya: Quick test: re-ran bench with pack-opt flags: `--pack-opt fused_vec --align 64`
```
pack=fused_vec align=64 -> token/s=2025, p95=50ms
```
So fused_vec + align fix much of the regression. But fused_vec requires extra memory transient during pack.

samir: Trade-offs: extra transient mem vs lower per-token cost. For hosted API we care p50/p99—favor fused kernels for latency-critical tiers; for Dedicated/Private we can use higher mem profiles. Add tiered policy.

maya: Also noticed KV cache behavior: if we repack buffers on first request and then mutate kv-cache pointers, we sometimes invalidate cached KV pages leading to extra memcpy on each step. Need to ensure repack doesn't touch runtime KV buffers.

elena: Suggestion: separate alloc arenas: one for packed static weights (oom-safe, long-lived) and one for KV cache (ephemeral). Do not share pages or move memory after we expose pointers to the runtime.

ci-bot: CI bench summary for PR#4893: int8-pack-update -> p99 regressions on small-seqs: +22% (slo-early) but +3% improvement on long-seqs (>2048).

maya: Actionable plan from my side:
- Stop repack-on-first-request; enqueue repack on background worker during model load (maya)
- Add LRU keyed by (model, qtype, group_size, align) for packed blobs (samir)
- Add validator to pack headers + force kernel ABI bits to avoid scalar fallback (elena)
- Update batching heuristics: require pack-amortize-threshold=4 before repacking per-request (maya)
- Add perf tests: microbench for pack time and small-batch p99 to CI matrix (perf-bot)

samir: I'll add the LRU PR tomorrow and wire a feature flag so we can A/B on prod.

elena: I'll take the kernel header validator and a small fuzzer to catch ABI mismatches.

maya: I'll push a quick revert of the repack-on-request path to unblock and then land the background repack + threshold.

maya: tagging @samir @elena for visibility, will follow up with numbers after the background repack lands. :thumbsup:
